initial_observation.demographics: A 63-year-old Saudi man, with no medical history and a 30-pack-year smoking history
initial_observation.encounter_context: Presented to the Emergency Department (ED) with weakness involving the left upper and lower limbs as well as a headache for the previous 2 weeks
initial_observation.chief_complaint: Weakness involving left upper and lower limbs and headache
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: A 63-year-old Saudi man with left-sided weakness and headache for 2 weeks, unintentional weight loss of 6 kg, lack of appetite, subjective fever, and night sweats. No cough, chest pain, shortness of breath, or hemoptysis. Denied other neurological symptoms. Vital signs stable, conscious and coherent with GCS 15/15. Left-sided weakness graded 4/5 in upper limb and 3/5 in lower limb. Clubbed fingers noted.
presenting_symptoms: left upper and lower limb weakness
known_prior_history: family history: patient’s brother died from laryngeal cancer

evidence_items.source_text: On the clinical examination, the patient was vitally stable, conscious, and coherent. He scored 15 of 15 on the Glasgow Coma Scale. The pupils were bilaterally equally reactive, at 3 mm. The cranial nerves were intact. On the hand examination, clubbed fingers were identified. The patient had left-sided weakness in the upper and lower limbs, with grades 4 of 5 and 3 of 5, respectively.
The results of his complete blood count, liver function tests, renal function tests, amylase, lipase, and serum calcium all were within the normal range.
A non-contrast computed tomography (CT) scan of the brain showed lesions with vasogenic edema in the right parietal lobe (Figure 1).
A chest X-ray showed right lung opacity, suggesting a mass in the right upper lobe of the lung (Figure 2).
A CT scan of the chest showed a mass in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe (Figure 3), and CT scan of the abdomen showed multiple hypodense liver lesions, indicating metastasis (Figure 4).

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain showed evidence of 2 ring-enhancing lesions within the right temporal and right parietal region, with extensive perifocal edema showing mild diffusion restriction and mid-line shift towards the left side (Figure 5).

A bronchoscopy was unremarkable. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration was done, and the biopsy was taken from the 4R lymph node; a total of 6 specimens were taken. Three specimens were stained with Diff-Quik stain and 3 were prepared unstained. The slides were fixed by Spray-Cyte and sent to the Pathology Laboratory, which showed that the patient’s sample was positive for malignancy, since there were clusters of malignant epithelial cells with enlarged hyperchromatic pleomorphic nuclei with coarse chromatin. Cell-block immunostaining showed positive reactivity of the malignant cells to CK-7, TTF-1, and focally for Napsin-A. These findings indicated primary lung adenocarcinoma.

The patient was admitted to the hospital for a malignancy workup with weakness in the left side of the body. Dexamethasone was started at a loading dose of 10 mg intravenously and continued on a regular dose, and levetiracetam 500 mg orally was started for prophylaxis to prevent convulsions. The patient followed up with the Oncology Department for staging and prognosis. Afterward, the patient was referred to the Palliative Care team.

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: The patient had stage IV metastatic lung adenocarcinoma.
accepted_aliases: lung adenocarcinoma with brain and liver metastases
primary lung adenocarcinoma with brain metastasis
